about: The OS function table a native (ELF) module is built against (docs/os_2026-11/tiers.md section 1): one row per function the kernel exports, its ORDINAL its index here. Rows are APPENDED, never changed, moved or removed; a row that goes is RETIRED and keeps its slot, answering through a typed stub. version counts the rows ever appended, so it is the table's length. name is the function's name in a module's source; c its prototype exactly as the module's C library headers declare it (posix rows, from the headers in hdr) or as sdk/include/moybyte/os.h declares it (moybyte rows); va, on a row whose prototype ends in ..., the one argument the kernel takes in its place and when the module passes it; glibc the name glibc's headers call the same function by (the host's modules); fail what the typed stub of a retired row answers (errno ENOSYS), null for a function that returns nothing; noreturn a function that does not return; retired the date and the reason. tools/gen_os_table.py writes the kernel's table (native/moy_elf/moy_os_table.h, .c) and the SDK's header and stubs (sdk/include/moybyte/os.h, sdk/src/moyos_stubs.c) from this; tests/test_os_table.py holds the outputs to it and the rows to their frozen copy.
